contract: Osc 1 offers Sine, Triangle, Shark Tooth, Saturated, Saw, Pulse and Rectangle; Osc 2 offers Sine, Triangle, Saturated, Saw and Rectangle.
Osc 1 Oct transposes octaves and Shape changes its waveform display; Osc 2 Oct transposes octaves and Detune uses semitones. Combined display includes enabled oscillator/noise output.

Osc 1 Shape sources are Env 1, Env 2/Cyc, LFO, Key, Velocity, Modwheel, Pressure and Slide. Shape Mod Amount spans -100% to 100%; positive Shape Mod can act even with Shape 0%. Key modulation reverses direction with amount sign.
Two pitch modulation sources affect both oscillators, each with amount -100% to 100%; Ratio-mode LFO pitch modulation is documented as able to produce FM tones.
Osc 1, Osc 2 and white-noise generator have independent enables/gains and individual filter-routing arrows. Routing off bypasses the filter for that source.
The manual describes oscillator gain -6 dB and saturation changes above 0 dB in the filter path; it supplies no transfer curve or measured thresholds for this build.
Oscillator R on resets both oscillator phases at each note; R off is free-running.

Low-pass Type I is labelled 12 dB/octave and Type II 24 dB/octave. Freq/Res and high-pass HP are separate; display dots adjust HP horizontally and LP frequency/resonance horizontally/vertically. Key 0.00 disables note influence on LP frequency; 1.00 follows note direction.
Two independent low-pass cutoff modulation slots each have amount -100% to 100%.

Envelope 1 controls amplitude of both oscillators and noise; Attack reaches peak, Decay reaches Sustain, Sustain holds until note ends, Release returns to zero. Knobs/display and 1/2 selectors edit the selected envelope.
Env 2 is a modulation source and can switch ADSR to Cycling; Cycling restarts on each MIDI note, offers Tilt/Hold and Rate/Ratio/Time/Sync using Hz/ratio/ms/beat divisions.

LFO time modes are Rate, Ratio, Time and Sync. Nine waveforms include Sine, Triangle, Saw Up/Down, Square, Sample & Hold, Wander, Linear Envelope and Exponential Envelope. R resets per note; off free-runs; Amount and its modulation source/depth control intensity.

Mod section has up to three source/destination slots with -100% to 100% amount. Sources are Env 1, Env 2/Cyc, LFO, Key, Velocity, Modwheel, Pressure, Slide; destinations include oscillator gains/shape/detune, Noise Gain, LP Frequency/Resonance, HP Frequency, LFO/Cyc rate and Main Volume.

Voice modes Poly, Mono, Stereo and Unison use respectively one, up to four, two and four voices per note. At Voices 32, Poly/Stereo/Unison permit 32/16/8 notes. Mono Thickness 0 uses one audible voice; new held-note onset chokes the previous note.
Drift changes per-voice oscillator and filter variation; no seed, distribution, repeatability or exact zero-variation law is supplied.
Mono Legato allows a new held-overlap note to change pitch without restarting envelopes; Glide sets overlapping-note pitch-slide time.
Volume and Vel > Vol control output/velocity; Transpose spans -48 to +48 semitones. Note PB toggles per-note pitch bend independently of global PB Range.

Browser double-click or waveform drag/drop loads a sample. Start and Length use percentages of total sample length; Shift-drag Start gives fine adjustment and waveform zoom. Start/Length/Gain update the display.
Sample Gain spans -70 to +24 dB, Transpose -48 to +48 semitones, Detune -50 to +50 cents, global Volume -36 to +36 dB. Pan changes stereo position and Velocity to Volume controls velocity response.
Trigger uses Attack/Hold/Decay and continues through Hold after note release; Hold inf plays the full sample. Gate disables Hold and starts Decay at note release.

Next/Previous Similar Sample cycle related samples; Show Similar Files opens browser results; Return to Reference returns to initial reference and Save as Similarity Reference replaces it. Waveform hot-swap replaces sample; title hot-swap replaces instrument.
Playback Effect On gates nine choices: Stretch, Loop, Pitch Env, Punch, 8-Bit, FM, Ring Mod, Sub Osc and Noise. Each has two controls; X/Y vertical edits first, horizontal second.
Stretch changes sample length without intended pitch change; Factor is a speed multiple and Grain Size uses milliseconds. Exact grain/window/interpolation law is unknown.
Loop repeats a sample region; Loop Offset is relative to sample start and Loop Length is milliseconds.
Pitch Env Amount -100% to +100% sets signed pitch change and Decay returns to base pitch defined by global controls.
Punch applies transient ducking; Amount controls reduction and Release controls return to zero gain reduction. Exact attack/envelope law is unknown.
8-Bit offers Sample Rate and Decay Time for its low-pass behavior; no bit-depth/aliasing/kernel equivalence follows from the name.

FM modulates sample pitch with a sine; Ring Mod modulates amplitude with low-rate tremolo and higher-rate ring-modulation character. Both have Amount/Frequency and modulation decay follows global Decay.
Sub Osc and Noise layer a generator following device Attack/Decay. Sub Frequency spans 30-120 Hz; Noise Color filters noise.
Time/frequency controls of Stretch, Loop, FM, Ring Mod, Sub Osc and Noise follow global pitch and played MIDI pitch; exact scaling is not supplied.
Filter On gates four types: 12 dB LP, 24 dB LP, 24 dB HP and Peak. LP/HP expose Resonance/Frequency; Peak exposes Peak Gain/Frequency.
Mod source is Velocity or Slide (MPE); destinations are Filter, Attack, Hold, Decay, FX1 and FX2. FX1/FX2 address current effect controls; amount controls depth.
Enable Per-Note Pitch Bend is documented enabled by default. Envelope Follows Pitch scales envelope relative to sample pitch so it affects the same portion when transposed.
Drum Sampler > Simpler replaces the instrument retaining sample Start and Length positions; other parameter translations are not established.
Save as Default Pad from a Drum Rack pad context makes new samples on empty pads load Drum Sampler.
Expanded View reveals all modulation sources/targets; A/B selects engine matrix, Copy to A/B copies modulation values and X clears active modulation values.
Engines A/B enable independently. Disabling an engine deactivates its filter; a filter can be disabled without disabling its engine.
Engine Octaves/Semitones/Cents pitch controls become scale-degree transposition when Use Current Scale follows Live Scale Mode; Pitch Quant target is included.

Oscillator macros depend on selected type: Basic Shapes Shape/Tone; Dual Basic Shapes Shape/Detune; Noisy Shapes Shape/Rough; Square Sync Freq 1/2; Square 5th 5th Amt/P Width; Sub Tone/Aux; four Swarms Motion/Spacing; Harmonic Fm Amount/Ratio; Fold Fm Amount/Shape; Squelch Amount/Feedback; Simple Fm Amount/Ratio; Chip Tone/Rate. Overview type count is unresolved.
Shepard’s Pi Rate 0.0-49.9 descends, 50.0 has no movement, 50.1-100.0 ascends; Width changes octave count.

Remaining described macros are Tarp Decay/Tone; Extratone Pitch/Env Amount; Noise Loop Rate/Fade; Filtered Noise Freq/Width; Bitgrunge Freq/Mult; Crackle Density/Intensity; Rain Tone/Rate; Bubble Density/Spread; Chord Shape/Inversion. Named descriptions do not prove kernels or RNG.

Chord uses four sawtooth oscillators with Shape intervals and Inversion order. With Use Current Scale, chords use selected scale; with no scale set, incoming root uses major. Availability/version/context remains unresolved.

Amp/Mod envelopes offer ADSR and slopes; Trigger plays all segments ignoring Sustain, Loop repeats entire envelope without holding Sustain, AD Loop repeats Attack/Decay. Mod envelope adds Initial/Peak/Final.
Link Envelopes links corresponding engine Amplitude and Modulation envelopes.

Each engine has LFO 1 and 2 with Hz/sync, Phase Offset and Retrigger. LFO 1 types are Basic Shapes, Ramp, Wander, Alternate, Euclid, Pulsate; FX1/2 each describe eighteen serial effects. LFO 1 and processed LFO1 FX are separate sources. LFO 2 offers Sine, Tri, Saw Up/Down, Rectangle, Random S&H.

Matrix source columns/target rows accept signed modulation. Clicking parameter adds it to selected engine matrix; unmodulated temporary row disappears on next selection. Additive/multiplicative target assignment and complete units remain U.

Velocity and Pitch sources use note values for that note duration; Random gets new value at note trigger. MIDI Pitch Bend/Press/Wheel and MPE Note Pitch Bend/Slide/Press supply sources, including clip envelopes.
Osc Key Tracking off produces C3 constant pitch, or scale root in C3 octave when scale mode active; on follows incoming note.
Phase Reset enables Phase Spread. With Reset on, Spread off sets start phase zero; Spread on follows Spread matrix source.

Oscillator Scale Awareness lists Dual Basic Shapes, Swarm Sine/Triangle/Saw/Square and Chip. Filter Scale Awareness lists Plate and Membrane Resonators. These per-engine settings are distinct from Use Current Scale.
Portamento slides continuously and Glissando in discrete steps, using scale degrees when scale awareness is on. Both Mono and Poly permit Glide, audible only with Glide Time above zero.

Filter types have Frequency and type-dependent macros. SVF 12/24 L-B-H-N morphs LP/BP/HP/notch; MS2 LP/HP, OSR BP, LP Crunch, LP Switched Res Lofi and Filther are described. Q emphasizes cutoff and Drive saturates input.
Eq Peak Boost/width and Eq Notch Cut/width, Phaser Feedback/Spread, Redux Crush/Lofi, Vowel Morph and Comb +/- Feedback/Damp have distinct roles.
Plate and Membrane Resonators describe first 32 modes of rectangular plate/circular membrane and scale-following resonant frequencies with Filter Scale Awareness.
Per-engine Volume/Pan and Tone Filter are separate; positive Tone reduces lows and negative Tone reduces highs.
Mixer Drive is per voice after engine mixer settings and before per-voice limiter; Limit gates limiter after both engines mixed and global Drive applied. Global Volume sets output.
Mono permits Legato: overlap with Legato on reuses current envelope position, off restarts envelope. Poly exposes 2-12 voices.
Stacked Voices duplicates both engines including filters/modulation/mix. Spread offsets stacked voices, or notes in held chord when Stacked Voices Off. Spread has no effect without a matrix target.
The matrix paragraph says negative values speed envelopes/LFOs and positive slow them, but the applicable target/preconditions are unspecified; do not generalize that statement to all destinations.
Four oscillators use eleven predefined algorithms; icons describe top-to-bottom routing. Algorithm selector supports MIDI mapping, automation and real-time modulation.

Wave chooser includes sine, resynthesized saw/square/triangle variants, Sine 4/8 Bit, Saw D, Square D, Noise Looped, Noise White and User. Numeric harmonic names denote retained harmonic counts, not exact output samples.

Harmonics editor offers 16/32/64 partials, Shift constrains editing to one harmonic, Repeat off truncates above chosen count, even/odd/all drawing and Normalize; waveform copy/paste works across oscillators.
Waveform context exports .ams to User Library Samples/Waveforms; browser drag imports .ams into an oscillator; Simpler/Sampler are also documented consumers.

Osc Coarse/Fine set note-relative ratios; Fixed replaces controls with Frequency Hz and Multiplier and ignores note pitch, with described low endpoint 0.1 Hz. The manual states fixed frequency is Freq multiplied by Multi; no note-frequency formula is supplied.
Osc < Vel controls signed velocity pitch response; Q quantizes it as Coarse changes.
Each oscillator Level/envelope responds to Vel/Key; Phase and R control note-start phase/free-run. Feedback acts only on oscillators not modulated by another oscillator.

Antialias and Interpolation are independently selectable, Tone affects high-frequency content. Manual new-patch default Antialias on does not prove installed constructor/preset defaults or a numerical alias bound.

LFO routes Dest A to selected oscillators/filter and Dest B to one extra target; global Amount, Vel and envelope scale depths. Range Low describes 50 seconds-30 Hz, Hi 8 Hz-12 kHz and Sync tempo; R resets/free-runs; Rate < Key 100% doubles per octave.

Seven envelopes cover oscillators/filter/pitch/LFO; oscillator Attack is documented linear and Decay/Release exponential, ending -inf dB. Filter/pitch slopes and End vary. Note Off starts Release from current value. Shapes copy across oscillators.

Envelope modes include Loop, Beat, Sync and Trigger. Beat repeats note-relative without quantizing notes; Sync first repeat nearest sixteenth while song plays, otherwise Beat-like. Trigger ignores Note Off. Loop restart level is unresolved.

Loop restart wording differs: overview says current level to peak, Loop Time listing says sustain-to-initial then restart, Beat/Sync listing says current-to-peak. Applicability to the same mode/preconditions is unresolved.
Global Time, Time < Key and per-envelope Time < Vel scale envelope segments; Beat/Sync repetition beat-time is not changed by global Time or Time < Vel.
Pitch envelope can target A-D and LFO via Dest A and another Dest B; amount +100% follows levels and -100% inverts sign; envelope On gates it.

Filter types LP/HP/BP/notch/Morph offer 12/24 dB slopes. Clean/OSR apply all types; MS2/SMP/PRD LP/HP. Non-Clean LP/HP/BP expose Drive. Morph sweeps LP/BP/HP/notch and context snaps to named responses.
Filter Frequency responds to velocity/key/envelope/LFO; key 100% doubles per octave around C3. Play by Key sets Freq 466 Hz and Freq < Key 100%; this command is distinct from a global tuning formula.
Shaper chooser/Drive act on filtered path; Dry/Wet 0% bypasses shaper and shaper drive.

Voices supports up to 32; excess notes cut oldest notes. Voices 1 plays overlapping notes legato without retriggering envelopes. Global R retriggers an already enabled note rather than adding a voice.

Velocity, Key, Aftertouch, Pitch Bend and Mod Wheel each route to two targets with independent amounts; fixed Time < Key and PB Range coexist. Targets include Off, oscillator volume/crossfades/feedback/fixed pitch/FM Drive, filter controls, shaper, LFO, pitch envelope, Volume/Pan/Tone/Time; eligibility is target-specific.
Glide is polyphonic, starts new note at prior-note pitch then slides; legato Glide does not retrigger envelopes; Glide Time has no effect if Glide off.
Spread uses two detuned voices per note panned L/R; whether a note uses Spread is determined at Note On.
Transpose changes already-playing notes. Context commands copy oscillator parameters, set all envelope levels to maximum/minimum/middle, edit harmonics and export .ams.
Enable Per-Note Pitch Bend is documented on by default and can be disabled in device-title context.

Two oscillators enable independently; tabs select editing, expanded view redistributes controls. Gain/Pan/Semi/Detune are per oscillator. Category/table choosers and arrows traverse category boundaries.
Dropping WAV/AIFF on visualization imports it; choosers/arrows then browse its folder. Raw bypasses automatic sample preprocessing.
Dragging visualization or Wave Position selects table position. Linear/polar show same data with distinct layouts.

Oscillator effects are FM (Amt/Tune), Classic (PW/Sync), Modern (Warp/Fold). Two effect values persist across effect-type changes. FM Tune +/-50% and +/-100% describe +/-1 and +/-2 octave modulator offsets.
Sub enables independently with Gain, Tone 0% sine/increasing harmonics, and one/two octave-down switches relative to note/global Transpose.

Each filter offers LP/HP/BP/notch/Morph, 12/24 dB slopes; Clean/OSR all types and MS2/SMP/PRD LP/HP. Non-Clean LP/HP/BP expose Drive. Display dots adjust Frequency/Resonance; Morph traverses LP/BP/HP/notch.

Serial sends mains through Filter 1 then 2; Parallel feeds mains to both; Split assigns Osc 1/2 to Filter 1/2 and halves Sub to both. Split leaves corresponding oscillator audible when its filter is off.

Matrix uses source columns/target rows. Additive values sum then add to parameter, neutral 0; multiplicative values multiply then multiply parameter, neutral 1 minimum 0. Source units, depth scaling, clamps and each target assignment remain unresolved except explicit labels.
Clicked parameter appears temporarily; nonzero modulation keeps its row, otherwise next selected parameter replaces it. Matrix and MIDI tabs share rows; source headers jump to source panels.
Time scales all modulator times, negative faster/positive slower. A modulator assigned to Time does not scale itself through that route but still scales other destinations.
Global Matrix Amount, LFO Amount, instrument Volume and Unison Amount are documented multiplicative destinations.

Amp, Env2 and Env3 have Time/Slope; Env2/3 also Initial/Peak/Final, absent on Amp. Positive slopes start fast then slow; negative slow then fast; zero linear. Sustain/Initial are documented multiplicative where present.
Envelope None holds Sustain until Note Off; Trigger plays all segments at Note On; Loop repeats whole envelope without Sustain hold until voice ends.
Two LFOs offer Sine, Saw, Triangle, Square and Random with waveform-dependent Shape. Sync switches rate Hz/beat divisions.
LFO Offset sets start phase and cannot be modulated; Attack fades in after Note On; Retrigger resets phase on each new note.
MIDI Velocity/Note apply through note duration; Note 100% Filter Frequency tracks pitch around C3. Pitch Bend/Aftertouch/Wheel can use clip envelopes; Random samples at each new note.
Transpose uses semitones; Mono is single voice with legato envelopes and permits Glide; Poly enables Poly Voices and disables Glide.
Unison choices are none, Classic, Shimmer, Noise, Phase Sync, Position spread and Random note. They differ in detune, phase reset, stereo and position/randomization roles.
Unison Voices controls oscillators per main wavetable oscillator; Amount is mode-dependent intensity, distinct from Poly Voices note count.
Hi-Quality context switch controls quality; off is documented modulation every 32 samples and lower-power filters. CPU saving up to 25% is a conditional manual claim, not a required timing benchmark.

As of Live 11.1 the manual describes Hi-Quality off for new/Core Library instances while earlier user presets/Sets retain on for consistency; enabling may produce subtle differences. Migration boundaries for this target are unresolved.
Manual claims unmodulated raw oscillator output is band-limited with no aliasing at any pitch. No spectral measurement definition, finite pitch-domain fixture or tolerance accompanies this claim.
